# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Dwarf bamboo (*Sasa* spp.) forms dense evergreen stands that exclude subordinate species, and its expansion into alpine snowbed vegetation threatens plant diversity in Japanese mountains. Because alpine vegetation and snowmelt vary over distances of metres, observing this expansion requires approximately 1 m resolution, which neither field plots nor satellites provide across whole slopes. We asked two questions: is the expansion of *Sasa* limited mainly by environmental conditions, in particular snowmelt timing, or by its ability to reach suitable sites, and which plant communities does its near-term expansion threaten? Using 10 years of ground-based time-lapse imagery of an alpine slope on Mt. Tateyama, Japan, we mapped *Sasa* at 1 m resolution in 2012 and 2021, derived the mean snowmelt date of every cell, fitted a habitat suitability model and an establishment model of the observed 2012–2021 changes, and projected establishment to 2030 with a simulation that advances patch fronts annually. *Sasa* area changed by +19% over 9 years (gross expansion 48%, gross loss 29%, the loss concentrated at ambiguous boundaries with dwarf pine). Establishment probability was most strongly associated with distance from existing patches, approximately 10% within 5 m of the front and below 1% beyond 10 m, together with a favourable snowmelt window (mean snowmelt date approximately day of year 150–185). Environmentally suitable area was approximately 16 times the occupied area, suggesting that dispersal, rather than habitat availability, limits the current distribution. Projected establishment by 2030 was approximately 4,900–5,700 m², comparable to the observed decade, and nine tenths of it fell in two snowbed communities adjoining existing patches. Near-term expansion is therefore spatially predictable: removal or containment at patch fronts bordering snowbeds, complemented by surveillance of suitable areas for establishment from seed, offers a concrete conservation strategy.

# Data Availability Statement {.unnumbered}

The imagery-derived vegetation and snowmelt rasters, terrain predictors, all fitted model objects, projection outputs, and scripted analysis pipeline with its acceptance tests are permanently archived at Zenodo (<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22745234>). A development mirror is maintained at <https://github.com/0kam/SasaSDMPaper>.
